question: True or false: lecithin is the molecule doing most of the emulsifying in an egg-yolk mayonnaise?
answer: False. The main workers are low-density lipoproteins, tiny balls of protein and phospholipid in the yolk. At the oil surface they burst open and spread their proteins and phospholipids together into a film tougher than either alone. Lecithin, the textbook molecule, is one member of the team.
move: A single named cause is often a team with one famous member.
ask: What do I credit to one famous cause when many causes are behind it?
trap: True, because lecithin is the emulsifier every label and textbook names.
reference: Anton, Egg yolk: structures, functionalities and processes, Journal of the Science of Food and Agriculture, 2013
